newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon plans to buy 50,000 tonnes hard wheat.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon plans to buy 50,000 tonnes hard wheat.

text.p: Lebanon's economy ministry plans to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later this month on the international market, an official of the Cereals and Sugar Beet Office said on Wednesday.
"We plan to buy 50,000 tonnes of wheat. It will be Hard Red Winter No.2," the official told Reuters.
"We are supposed to buy it later this month for delivery at the end of February but we still do not have all the details for the tenders."
The cereals office is part of the economy ministry, which last year made purchases of 200,000 tonnes of wheat through local agents of international firms.
Lebanon has yearly requirements of about 400,000 tonnes of wheat.
"We still have some 40,000 to 50,000 tonnes of wheat in storage at the (Beirut port) silos and this should last us three or four months but we also like to buy in advance," the official added.

The last wheat purchases by the ministry were in June, when the Beirut agent for international grain trading firm MAPCO won a bid to supply 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat at $245.45 per tonne and the agent for Swiss-based Cargill Inc won a bid to supply 25,000 tonnes of soft U.S. wheat at $211.93 per tonne.
The ministry periodically invites local agents of international firms to tender to buy wheat on behalf of the government. The firms also buy wheat for the private sector.
